evidence.where: Appendix H, p. H-28, caption (continued on H-29)

evidence.quote: Table H-7A Sub-Table for Maritime Life Rafts with Deep Ballast Systems and Canopies
The Slope coefficient is dimensionless and the Y-intercept has units of nautical miles per hour [kts].
the original maximum values were divided by 1.35 and rounded up to the nearest degree to provide the average values appearing in this appendix
evidence.where: Appendix H, section H.3.4.7(f), p. H-27

evidence.quote: Y-intercept (in knots) was rounded to nearest 0.01 knots (0.5 cm/s).
evidence.where: Appendix H, section H.3.4.7(a), p. H-27

tried: The PDF's built-in viewer could not be driven, and page rendering stalls while the browser pane is hidden, so rows were rebuilt from the text layer's x/y positions (every row on pp. H-28 to H-30 aligned cleanly into class, slope, intercept, angle and standard-error columns).
notes: Edition: COMDTINST M16130.2F, January 2013, Appendix H. Units differ from the 1999 report: leeway speed in knots with a dimensionless slope and the intercept in knots; divergence is an average angle (the 1999 maximum divided by 1.35, section H.3.4.7(f)); a standard-error column in knots is added. The same classes as the 1999 bundle are transcribed so the two can be compared row by row, never merged. Section H.3.4.7 also records that 'Junk' was renamed 'Asian Coastal F/V' and two non-SAR classes were added back. A quick check of the conversion: the 1999 deceased-PIW intercept of 4.0 cm/s is 0.078 kt, which the Addendum prints as 0.08.
